execution: Ahead-of-time DCDart → Kernel IR → DC-IR → LLVM → WebAssembly. Source compilation happens at build time; inputs execute locally in a browser worker.

demos.title: Count it up
demos.label: 01 / Loops
demos.description: A while loop, two fixed-width integers, and a running total. Sum every integer from zero up to (but excluding) n.

demos.title: A little unpredictability
demos.label: 02 / ARC + control flow
demos.description: Follow the Collatz sequence, or sum the steps through a heap-allocated counter. The compiled DCDart code allocates, updates, and releases that object.

demos.title: Down the call stack
demos.label: 03 / Recursion
demos.description: Allocate a box in each recursive call. Read its value and let DCDart’s generated ARC code release it. The live-allocation count should return to zero.

demos.title: Every bit accounted for
demos.label: 04 / Integers
demos.description: Real unsigned 64-bit arithmetic, including values beyond JavaScript’s safe integer range. Overflow and integer division by zero trap.

demos.title: Room for a fraction
demos.label: 05 / Floating point
demos.description: IEEE-754 arithmetic emitted by the same compiler. Floating-point division by zero produces Infinity or NaN; integer division traps.
